props.gloss_en: how much [must be cut for] a severed windpipe? its majority
Rav: [the majority is] the majority of its thickness
and some report [Rav as saying]: the majority of its hollow
a severed windpipe came before Rav, and he sat and checked it by the majority of its thickness
Rabba bar bar Chana checked it by the majority of its hollow and declared it fit
and he bought meat from it for thirteen plain istera
a sage who declared impure -- his fellow may not declare pure; who forbade -- his fellow may not permit
'my soul has not been made impure' -- I did not think by day so as to come to impurity at night
'neveila and tereifa I have not eaten' -- I never ate the meat of a 'slaughter it, slaughter it' animal
'no piggul meat came into my mouth' -- I did not eat from an animal on which a sage ruled
in R' Natan's name they said: I did not eat from an animal whose [priestly] gifts were not separated
that applies to a matter that depends on reasoning; Rabba bar bar Chana relied on his received learning
one who judged, acquitted or convicted, declared impure or pure, forbade or permitted, and likewise witnesses who testified -- all may buy
but the Sages said: distance yourself from the unseemly and from what resembles it
that applies to a thing sold by appraisal; here the scale proves [the price]
Rabba permitted a [questioned] tereifa and bought meat from it
Father permitted a firstborn and did not buy meat from it
what is there [to suspect] -- a choice cut? every day they sell me a choice cut
who is a Torah scholar? one who sees [rules on] a tereifa for himself
who is 'he who hates gifts shall live' (Prov 15:27)? one who sees a tereifa for himself
whoever reads and studies, sees a tereifa for himself, and has served Torah scholars -- of him the verse says 'when you eat the labour of your hands, happy are you and it is well with you' (Ps 128:2)
Rav Zevid: he merits and inherits two worlds, this world and the world to come
'happy are you' -- in this world
'and it is well with you' -- in the world to come
R' Elazar: when they sent him something from the Nasi's house he did not take it, and when they invited him he did not go
R' Elazar: does the master not want me to live?
the verse: 'and he who hates gifts shall live' (Prov 15:27)
R' Zeira: when they sent to him he did not take, when they invited him he went
R' Zeira: it is they who are honoured by me
[a windpipe] perforated like a sieve -- [the holes] join toward the majority
a skull with one long hole, or even with many holes -- they join to the full size of a drill-hole
holes that involve a deficiency join to an issar; those without deficiency join to the majority
a strip was removed from it -- it joins to an issar
a windpipe perforated like a sieve -- what is [its law]?
in a bird, what [is the measure]?
one folds it and lays it on the mouth of the windpipe: if it covers the majority of the windpipe, tereifa; if not, fit
Rav Pappa: and your mnemonic is a sieve
[the windpipe] was broken open like a door -- [the measure is] enough for an issar to enter its width
[the windpipe] was cracked -- even if only one ring remained above and one ring below, it is fit
rather say: even if only something remained above and something below, it is fit
the whole neck is fit for slaughter, from the great ring to the lower lobes of the lung
Rava: the 'lower' [lobes] which are the upper
for I say: whatever [extent] it stretches its neck and grazes, provided it is not forced
if he forced [the neck] at the simanim and slaughtered -- [the slaughter] is invalid
a windpipe perforated below the chazeh is judged as the lung
which is the chazeh? the part that faces the ground; below as far as the neck, above as far as the rumen
one cuts two ribs from the two sides, this way and that, and this is the chazeh given to the priests
